summary: Maurice Bloomfield was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Chicago, Furman, South Carolina, Princeton, Yale under Whitney, and Johns Hopkins under Lanman. He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Grammont was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (ca. 1888-1892) under Ferdinand de Saussure (ca. 1889-1891). He held a post at the University of Montpellier from ca. 1895 to 1939.
Maurice Jametel was a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and later held a post there from circa 1886 to 1889.
Maurice O'Connell Walshe was a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Walpola Rahula. He held a post at the University of London.
Maurice Wiles was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tonbridge School (ca. 1937-1942) and Christ's College, Cambridge (ca. 1947-1950).

Maurine Stuart was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Manitoba, with Nadia Boulanger, and under Zen teachers Eido Shimano, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, and Soen Nakagawa. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

Mauro Maggi works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Naples "L'Orientale," directed the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East, and held posts at IsIAO and Sapienza University of Rome.

Mavis L. Fenn studied English at Winnipeg, religious studies at Calgary, and earned a Ph.D. under Graeme MacQueen at McMaster. A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, she taught at St. Paul's University College and Waterloo.

Max Deeg is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology scholar who completed his Habilitation at the University of Würzburg. He headed the School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University and is a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Max Kaltenmark was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He directed the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études Sinologiques (1946) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1949-1953), and held posts at the EPHE and the University of Paris (ca. 1957-1979).

Max Leopold Margolis was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. Educated at Leibniz-Gymnasium Berlin and Columbia (Ph.D. 1891), he held faculty posts at Hebrew Union College, the University of California, Berkeley, and Dropsie College (1909-1932).
Max Lindenau studied at the University of Leipzig until 1913 under Ernst Windisch.

Max Oidtmann is a historian, sinologist, and tibetologist educated at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard under Mark Elliott. He taught at Georgetown University and Georgetown University in Qatar (2013-2021) before becoming a professor at the University of Munich in 2021.

Max Scheler was a philosopher who studied at Munich, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Jena. He held academic posts at Jena (ca. 1900-1906), Munich (ca. 1907-1910), Göttingen (ca. 1910-1911), and Cologne (ca. 1919-1928).

Max Walleser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nuremberg, taught at Heidelberg University (1911; 1918-1936), and founded the Heidelberg Institute for Buddhology in 1928.
May Oung was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at the University of Cambridge from ca. 1904 to 1907. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910.

Maya Jasanoff is a historian who studied at Harvard College, the University of Cambridge, and Yale University. She held a post at the University of Virginia (ca. 2003-2009) and became a history professor at Harvard University ca. 2009.
Mayum Chonying Wangmo Dorji was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as a member of its General Council from 1964 to 1965.

Mayumi Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She held teaching appointments as a lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2011-2013) and as a specially appointed associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

McKim Marriott was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Harvard, under Clyde Kluckhohn, and at the University of Chicago (PhD ca. 1949-1955). He served as a professor of anthropology and social sciences at Chicago from ca. 1955-1998.
